> **Editorial pass: specification, not textbook.** .... compute, check, or reject.

I generally agree with this, and I might go further given the scale of the changes:

I think we need a spec that is written separately from the NUTs PRs. This spec will be complete and very clear. Then, after we all fully understand and approve the spec, we can ask ourselves _"do the PRs to the NUTs repo give effect to the spec?"_

This separate spec docs would:
 - minimize any discussion of justification or motivation, and will instead focus on facts of what to "compute, check, or reject"
 - make clear that no changes are being introduced to the rules for software that doesn't yet support v3. i.e. no breaking changes
 - make clear which mint/melts/swaps are allowed based on the various combinations of the various kinds of inputs and outputs
 - make clear that nothing unnecessary is being added; we focus just on changes required for v3. For example, if we want to have a rule that says a given B_ can be signed just once, then that's not specific to v3 and it can be merged to the NUTs repo today; it's something that's already implemented by the mints anyway.
 - make clear how the various other functionality (e.g. NUT-07) is affected. i.e. it's not just mints/melts/swaps. No breaking changes
 - make very clear when we are just making a 'natural' modification to v3 (_"NUT-07 witness and state will have the same meaning as before, and will be available at the same time, but will return a v3 witness instead of a v1/v2 witness"_) or if something bigger/newer is introduced (_"NUT-07 shall also return the `input_digest`; this is new, as v1/v2 did not return the (SIG_ALL) message signed when spending the v1/v2 inputs"_)

> This PR carries policy changes beyond BLS + nutroot that appear to have no technical dependency on either.

Most of [this review comment](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/443#pullrequestreview-5913880255) reads root as if it governed pre-v3 deployments. It does not: `legacy/` is `main` byte for byte, and a mint serving only pre-v3 keysets follows it unchanged. I have now scoped the README's MUST to implementations that support v3 keysets so that is explicit at the top rather than only in `legacy/README.md`.

On the items:

1, 2, 3, 5. The mandatory table is the v3 one, and the README now says so in the sentence that carries the MUST. NUT-20 and NUT-10 are mandatory for v3, bolt11 `pubkey` is required for a v3 mint, and the discovery setting goes because there is nothing to discover: every v3 mint locks quotes. Legacy NUT-20 keeps `optional` and its setting, so no current deployment changes status at merge.
4. Fair. The 11/12/14 rows are back, under the README's Legacy heading, linking into `legacy/`.
6. 20008 is raised by the mint flow, which is where NUT-04 now defines the v3 signature; the row names both.
7. 11003 and 11004 are on `main` today (see `error_codes.md` there). The sentence names the rule the codes already enforce and nutshell and cdk already implement. It is not v3-specific, agreed, so it moves to its own PR on `main`: cashubtc/nuts#481. Same for the `secret` uniqueness sentence.

> **Editorial pass: specification, not textbook.**

Agreed on the principle [in this review comment](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/443#pullrequestreview-5913944655), and it is the one this PR was written to. The "WHY" lives in the design notes linked from the description; the NUT text is what to compute, check and reject. The sentences you flagged are leftovers and are gone or reduced to their rule. One I kept: the sentence mapping multisig, refund and HTLC onto leaf types, since it is the only place a NUT-11 or NUT-14 reader learns which leaf replaces their lock.

From [comment](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/443#issuecomment-6911996548): 
> I think we need a spec that is written separately from the NUTs PRs.

A separate spec already exists: the design notes linked from the description have carried the full model since the summer, with the Implementers Guide, vectors and three implementations on top. What is in this PR is the "compute, check or reject" text you describe, and a second document to approve first would restart review rather than finish it.

Your bullets are the right checklist, and the tree answers them: `legacy/` is `main` byte for byte, so pre-v3 rules do not change; the signing-rule table in NUT-00 now says what each input and output kind follows, so the combinations are in one place; NUT-07's `input_digest` is the one new field and is marked as such. `B_` uniqueness is not v3-specific, agreed, and moves to its own PR on `main` (cashubtc/nuts#481), where the per-keyset question can be argued on its own.

As discussed just now elsehwere, let's also include a clarifcation about NUT-09, such that it does it's lookup based only on B_, and it ignores the 'amount' and the 'keyset'. 

NUT-09 should return the amount and keyset that was actually signed for this B_

This behaviour is what's already implemented, and is already relied upon

I don't mind whether we do that in #481 or in this PR

> The error code rename

I didn't notice/remember that I had made other changes like that 😀.

Maybe I accidentally included other stuff. _(I did look at it with my human eyes, but maybe not as thoroughly as I should have)_

I'm kinda busy now, and can't really easily change this PR. I don't mind if you make/edit another PR. I think I basically want something like this:

- define global sign-once behavior by canonical B_, regardless of amount or keyset
- clarify the errors around this for signed and pending blinded points
 - require NUT-09 restore lookup to use B_ alone, ignoring the requested amount and keyset ID
 - require NUT-09 restore responses to return the amount and keyset ID actually issued
 - clarify that wallets may use any amount within NUT-13 seed recovery; or, more precisely, ensure that wallets don't assume that the mint cares about the number used in the recovery

@robwoodgate

A note for anyone reviewing this as 443...main: three lines that #371 added to pre-v3 text are not in this tree.

- NUT-02: the `unit` regex is stated for `01` as well as `02`. Root keeps the sentence as written, but `legacy/02.md` has no regex because `main` has none.
- NUT-01: a MUST for the 33-byte compressed secp256k1 key format on `00` and `01` keysets.
- NUT-13: "reject `blinding_factor == 0`" in the V2 derivation prose (`main` has it in the Python docstring only).

This is by design rather than an omission. `legacy/` is generated from `main` and checked byte for byte against it, and root carries v3 plus the mixed-keyset interop, so a pre-v3 rule only survives if it is on `main`. None of the three changes what an implementation does, so I have not opened PRs for them; if anyone wants one kept, it is a one-line PR to `main` and the snapshot regenerates with it.
Folded into cashubtc/nuts#460, which carries the same two sentences.

We should recommend that wallets send v2 by default, for the foreseeable future, even if the sender's wallet supports v3

This is because many receivers will be v2-only for a while, and wallets should be cautious and send only v2 unless they are sure that v3 is supported by the receiver

I don't want to be trying to get somebody into Cashu and then I send them some e-cash and they complain that it didn't work; very bad experience for a new user. Therefore, I'll be sending v2-only (and using only wallets that allow me to do this) at first.

At some point in the future, after there is sufficient adoption that most receivers can accept v3, then we can consider making v3 the default for sending and deprecating v2

@SatsAndSports  - I pushed the edits we discussed to your branch: #481's two sentences replace the NUT-00 section, the order sentence is gone from NUT-09, and `amount` and `id` are now optional in the restore request so a wallet can send just `B_`. Body updated to match and #481 closed. Shout if anything there isn't what you meant, but as it stands this PR is an ACK from me.

> We should recommend that wallets send v2 by default, for the foreseeable future, even if the sender's wallet supports v3

That isn't something for the spec, and I don't see how the adoption of v3 will be any different to the adoption of v2, v1 or v0 keysets, or any of the other major changes to spec that have happened over the last 2 years.

In all cases, the spec makes the latest the "default", and implementations decide how quickly they move along.

> A separate spec already exists: the design notes linked from the description have carried the full model since the summer,


It's a very interesting and useful doc, but it's not precise enough to cover the mixed cases that mints will be required to support for the foreseeable future. It's not clear enough that we can ask ourselves "Are the NUTs PRs correctly implementing the clear rules in the spec?"_ . It's a great doc, it just doesn't fill that role

====

Parts of that doc ([Nutroot spec](https://hackmd.io/jdOrJ1COQfOHOkguUF8YOg)) are assuming a v3-only world. For example, _"SIG_ALL, SIG_INPUTS, sigflag, ... all cease to exist."_


But SIG_ALL will be fully supported for some time, it's just banned for swaps/melts that involve at least one v3 input.

_"... the migration path is itself a mixed transaction: old inputs, v3 outputs."_

and _"One shared transcript per transaction, one BIP-340 signature over its own **input digest** "_

As v3 rolls out, I'd prefer a wallet which sends v2 (because I don't know if the receiver is ready for v2) and sends v3 change back to myself. Therefore migration isn't a simple "swap everything to v3 and never deal with v2 again".

> It's a great doc, it just doesn't fill that role

Agreed, and it was never meant to. The design notes are the rationale; the normative text is this tree, and that is what the question "do the PRs give effect to the spec?" is checked against. That shape was settled when the reorg went in: root carries the current specification, `legacy/` carries the pre-v3 specifications unchanged, and [README's Legacy section](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/blob/886e7599b274810ec4db0f87f12c73eed7d2e696/README.md?plain=1#L65) says which governs when. A second document ahead of the tree would be a third copy of the same rules to keep in step.

On the mixed cases: the tree does not assume a v3-only world, the notes do because they describe the end state. Verification is per input, so `SIG_ALL` stays exactly as `legacy/11.md` specifies it for pre-v3 inputs, and the [signing rule table in NUT-00](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/blob/886e7599b274810ec4db0f87f12c73eed7d2e696/00.md#the-signing-rule) states what each kind of input and output follows in one transaction. Your example, pre-v3 inputs sent on with v3 change back to yourself, is a swap under that table: the inputs follow their pre-v3 rules and each output follows its own keyset. If you find a combination the table does not answer, that is a concrete gap and I will fix it.
Superseded by #443, which now targets `main` and carries this branch's commits (its head `4fa6698` is in that history). The BLS discussion stays here.

Added a second commit for 25.md: its bolt12 example quote is locked to the same pubkey (03d56ce4...), but the PostMintBolt12Request example had no signature, so per NUT-20 a mint would reject it (20008). It now uses the same example key as 20.md and carries a valid BIP340 signature over msg_to_sign for that quote id and those outputs.

> I reviewed d9928f06 while implementing Nutroot v3 in CDK #2951 (https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/pull/2951).

Thanks @thesimplekid, that was a really useful pass. All eight changes are in d9ea05c through efaf0bd, vectors in cashubtc/cashu-ts#1508, the check example on main in #492.

For implementers syncing vectors: as at 10d8a69 the shared JSON (the NUT-10/28 worked examples, transcripts, tokens, the five-leaf fold and the NUT-29 duplicate-quote request) is cashubtc/cashu-ts@e82d6f819b761c4726f9c915dd6ad4d1439646ec `test/vectors/nutroot-v3.json`, from cashubtc/cashu-ts#1508. The spec copies it verbatim.
Closing: #422 redefines the check as best-effort and removes this section, so the fix belongs there.
